_note: Full-state repeatability claims judged by tools/d63_fullstate_repeatability_gate.py against the REAL D63 engine (drift_canary/full_state_repeatability.py, PR #2320). Empty claims = explicit DORMANT (never a false green). The first claim merged activates enforcement with zero new wiring. Claims are evidence declarations: the gate rebuilds the certificate from the claim's own bytes and cold-verifies with independent_verify — a claim the law refuses (REPEATABLE asserted over a broken invariant, malformed certificate bytes, cross-obligation certificate) is BLOCKED (exit 1); an untrustworthy manifest or a broken engine is BROKEN (exit 2).

_schema.obligation_id: the obligation the repeatability claim is about (must equal the certificate's own obligation_id — cross-obligation certificates are refused)
_schema.evidence_ref: link to the evidence (board comment, run log, check run)
_schema.asserts: REPEATABLE | NOT_REPEATABLE — what the claim asserts the certificate establishes
_schema.certificate: the serialized repeatability certificate as a JSON object (the gate re-serializes with sort_keys and cold-judges the bytes via independent_verify)

_example._comment: WORKED EXAMPLE — not an active claim. If registered as a claim asserting REPEATABLE, the gate BLOCKS it (exit 1): the AER-LIVE-008 authority-expiry certificate. Debt-positive every traversal, but the authority token expires after 50 traversals. The naive debt-gain-only checker wrongly declares it repeatable — D63 rejects it at repetition 51 with the minimal counterexample named: invariant breaks at repetition 51: authority_valid. This is the exact repeatability fraud D63 exists to prevent.

model_assumptions: AER-LIVE-008: each unserved round adds exactly 1 debt at zero budget cost; the authority token expires after 50 traversals unless renewed; the exit (audit/shutdown) needs valid authority, intact evidence, and budget covering the exit cost.
